title: Ghost and Debt
premise: Coral Joubert, a financial-crimes investigator who launders reputations for the powerful, traces a dead whistleblower's voiceprint to a server in Lagos and discovers a plot to sabotage a water-treatment facility during a global finance summit, disguised as infrastructure failure. As she follows the money, she falls for Elias Mwangi, the auditor whose testimony she was hired to bury, forcing her to choose between the debt she owes her employers and the lives at stake. In the end she burns her own career, exposes the attack minutes before it happens, and inherits not her clients' fortune but their enemies.
about_author: Lior Okonkwo is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing illicit flows across three continents before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who discover that every clean ledger hides a body.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She closes another reputation-laundering case for a discreet client, then receives an anonymous audio file: a dead man's voice reading account numbers. The beat is professional detachment beginning to crack — she recognizes the voice of a man she once helped disappear.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Running the voiceprint against closed archives, she finds it unlocks a dormant server in Lagos containing transaction trails pointing toward the summit's host city. Emotional beat: dread dressed as curiosity; she should delete the file and doesn't.

chapters.title: Terms of Employment
chapters.summary: Her handler Voss's POV. Voss learns Coral has touched the ghost file and quietly reassigns her to 'monitor' the investigation — meaning contain it. The beat is cold institutional menace: loyalty as a leash.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: Elias Mwangi's POV. In Nairobi, the auditor who survived an 'accident' that killed his colleague notices his frozen accounts have been mysteriously unfrozen — bait. He decides to walk into the trap anyway. Beat: grief weaponized into recklessness.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Coral and Elias independently trace the same shell company from opposite ends and collide in a Lisbon records office. Beat: wary recognition — two liars who each spot the other's craft instantly.

chapters.title: What She Was Hired to Bury
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Flashback interwoven with present: three years ago she wrote the report that discredited Elias's testimony. Now he stands in front of her, alive, and doesn't yet know her name on that document. Beat: guilt sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Facility
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He reveals the pattern: maintenance contracts funneled through shells all converge on the Halcyon Water Works outside the summit city. Someone bought access, not water. Beat: the horror of arithmetic — the numbers only make sense as sabotage.

chapters.title: Containment
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss offers Coral a promotion to make her complicit, and hints that Elias is a designated fall guy. Beat: seduction of safety; Coral accepts just enough to buy time, hating herself for how easily yes comes.

chapters.title: Night Audit
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Coral and Elias break into a subcontractor's office and copy the real maintenance logs. A close call with security forces them to hide together. Beat: intimacy forged in adrenaline — trust offered before it's earned.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Voice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Decoding the server fully, she finds the whistleblower recorded his own murder warning before dying. His final message names the operation: 'Dry Season.' Beat: mourning a man she helped erase, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, with Coral's flashback. We learn Coral took this career to pay her late father's debts — the same debts that built the network she now serves. Beat: the theme lands; survival itself was the first thing she sold.

chapters.title: Framed
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Interpol flags him for the Lisbon break-in using evidence too clean to be real. He realizes Coral's employer is building its scapegoat and confronts her. Beat: betrayal — he assumes she set him up; she can't prove otherwise.

chapters.title: Split
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Elias goes dark; Coral, ordered to confirm his guilt, instead falsifies the confirmation and buys him forty-eight hours. Beat: the point of no return — she commits her first deliberate crime against her own side.

chapters.title: Dry Season
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The sabotage timeline accelerates: the attack is scheduled for the summit's opening night, timed to look like pump failure. Voss suspects Coral and feeds her a false facility. Beat: hunter becoming hunted, told from the hunter's calm.

chapters.title: Reunion at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Coral finds Elias through the dead man's server backdoor; contractors find them both. A chase through the old docks ends with Elias saving her life after learning she wrote the report that ruined him. Beat: love and grievance held in the same hands.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She tells Elias everything — the buried testimony, the promotion, the false confirmation. He must decide whether her betrayal of the network outweighs her betrayal of him. Beat: raw honesty; forgiveness neither promised nor refused.

chapters.title: The Second Server
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Following the whistleblower's hint, they find the true target isn't Halcyon but the summit hotel's water system — Halcyon is the decoy Voss fed them. Beat: vertigo; the trap was aimed at them all along.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledger
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She uploads the entire network's records to journalists and regulators simultaneously, knowing it ends her career and paints a target on her back. Beat: liberation through self-destruction — the debt called due, paid in full.

chapters.title: Opening Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, rapid cuts. Summit begins; contractors move; Coral and Elias race security, protocol, and the clock to force an evacuation without triggering panic or alerting Voss. Beat: breathless escalation, every advantage stripped away.

chapters.title: Accident Averted
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They trigger a visible chemical alarm that forces evacuation minutes before contamination; Voss's team scrambles to erase themselves. Confrontation between Coral and Voss — she wins by having already published everything. Beat: cold triumph with blood price.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hearings begin; the network fractures; Coral testifies under immunity she barely trusts. Elias chooses to stand beside her publicly despite the ruined report. Beat: quiet repair — love chosen again, deliberately, in daylight.

chapters.title: Ghost and Debt
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. Unemployed, watched, and finally free, she receives a new anonymous file — the network's survivors know where she lives. She opens it anyway. Beat: inheritance complete; the price of survival is never finished being paid.
